title: AI makes law firms faster — clients want a discount
summary: The New York Times reports that as AI tools speed up legal work, clients are pushing their law firms for lower fees.

title: Microsoft quietly drops the Copilot+ label from new laptops
summary: Previously covered on 2026-09-26: Bloomberg reported Microsoft was rebooting Copilot and stepping back from the consumer chatbot race.

title: 485 chemicals in US pesticide products linked to breast cancer
summary: New research reported by The Guardian finds 485 chemicals used in US pesticide products that are linked to breast cancer.

title: A discovery about life's origins, made in an $80 motel room
summary: The New York Times tells the story of a scientist whose work in a cheap motel room led to a finding that could shed light on how life began.

title: A model that doesn't train beat tuned XGBoost 14 times out of 14
summary: A new benchmark write-up compares TabPFN and TabICL — pre-trained models that make predictions on a spreadsheet-style dataset without being trained on it — against XGBoost, the long-time standard for tabular data, carefully tuned.

title: GitHub made its site faster by shipping more CSS
summary: GitHub fully migrated github.

title: Claude Sonnet 5.5: faster and cheaper than Sonnet 5
summary: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.

title: Nvidia wants a watchdog chip next to every AI agent
summary: CNBC reports that Nvidia is pitching a dedicated "watchdog" chip designed to sit alongside AI agents — software that takes actions on its own rather than just answering questions.

title: GitHub's open-source AI agent found 24 Android security flaws
summary: GitHub's security team used its open-source AI security agent to uncover 24 vulnerabilities in Android, including critical bugs.

title: Holo4: an AI that operates computer programs the way you do
summary: H Company released Holo4, a family of models built to use software interfaces directly — clicking and typing through apps rather than relying on special connections.

title: Cloudflare launches a command-line tool built for AI agents
summary: Cloudflare released cf, a command-line tool for its services that it describes as "agentic" — designed to be driven by AI assistants as well as people.

title: Language models small enough for a browser tab — or a cluster of $5 chips
summary: Two hobby projects on Hacker News push AI onto tiny hardware.

title: Git 2.56 is out
summary: The open-source Git project released version 2.

title: GPT-6.1 Sol: near-top performance at a fifth of the price
summary: Previously covered on 2026-09-23: OpenAI released GPT-6 in two versions, Sol and Luna.

title: OpenAI introduces Dots, agents that stay on
summary: OpenAI announced Dots, which it describes as always-on agents.

title: NVIDIA releases a free model that predicts spreadsheet columns without training
summary: NVIDIA published Kumo Tabular, an open model for table-shaped data.

title: How Delhi cut electricity losses from 50% to 5%
summary: IEEE Spectrum looks at how Delhi reduced the share of electricity lost between the power plant and the customer from about half to about one in twenty.

title: Vermont is swapping power plants for home batteries
summary: The BBC reports on a "virtual power plant" in Vermont: batteries in ordinary homes, pooled together, that keep the lights on during storms.

title: Checking that an AI agent cited the right source, not just a true fact
summary: Multiverse Computing published ProvenanceGuard, a checker for AI agents that pull information from several tools at once.

title: Cloudflare is building a certificate authority for the whole internet
summary: Cloudflare wrote about building its own certificate authority — the kind of organisation that issues the certificates behind the padlock icon in your browser, which prove a website is who it claims to be.

title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon
summary: Google published an announcement for Gemini 4 Argon, a new model carrying the Gemini 4 name.

title: A maths app for kids where the AI gets it wrong on purpose
summary: Lathoa is a new maths app for children in which the AI tutor deliberately makes mistakes, and the child's job is to catch them.

title: Hugging Face launches a public scoreboard for AI voices
summary: Hugging Face opened the Open TTS Leaderboard, which compares text-to-speech models across many languages and on voice cloning, and lets people vote on which outputs sound best.

title: US cities are being made to share licence-plate data with a federal programme
summary: 404 Media reports that cities are being required to funnel data from their licence-plate cameras into a large federal surveillance programme known as HIDTA.

title: A researcher says 17 trillion Microsoft records were within reach
summary: A security researcher describes how they could have accessed 17 trillion Microsoft records through a flaw they found.

title: Netlify makes its Edge Functions 5x faster by switching sandboxes
summary: Netlify moved its Edge Functions — small pieces of code that run close to the visitor — from V8 isolates (the sandboxing approach browsers use for JavaScript) to Firecracker microVMs, lightweight virtual machines originally built by Amazon.

title: Hugging Face Transformers can now run llama.cpp's compressed models
summary: Hugging Face's Transformers library, the most widely used toolkit for working with open AI models, can now load quantized model files made for llama.

title: AI helps a historian find a new eyewitness record of the dodo
summary: A historian writes that they used Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.

title: Researchers study what your connected car knows about you
summary: A team at Northeastern University published "Automatic Transmission", a data-privacy study of connected vehicles.

title: OpenAI and Synopsys team up on AI for chip design
summary: OpenAI and Synopsys, a major maker of chip-design software, announced GPT-Synopsys, a model aimed at helping engineers design computer chips.

title: arXiv tightens how fast you can download papers
summary: arXiv, the free library where most AI and science research papers appear first, updated its rate-limit policy, which caps how many requests one visitor can make.

title: GitHub publishes new transparency data and a policy outlook
summary: GitHub released its latest transparency figures alongside an update on US state-level policy that affects developers and open-source projects.

title: Olmo-core 3: open tools for training very large AI models
summary: The Allen Institute for AI released Olmo-core 3, open-source training infrastructure built around mixture-of-experts (MoE) models — models that route each input to a few specialised sub-networks instead of using the whole model every time.

title: Cloudflare launches Clef: open decision models you can fine-tune
summary: Cloudflare announced Clef, a set of open-weight "decision models" — models built to choose between actions rather than write long answers — along with a new platform for fine-tuning them using reinforcement learning, a method where a model improves by being rewarded for good outcomes.

title: AI beats the best Stratego player in history — on a budget
summary: Ars Technica reports that an AI system has beaten the strongest Stratego player on record.

title: GitHub names three skills to strengthen as AI changes the job
summary: GitHub published advice for developers whose work is being reshaped by AI: learn to direct AI agents, review what they produce with a critical eye, and keep your own judgment at the centre of the work.

title: Court sides with EFF: Utah's VPN law asks for the impossible
summary: A court agreed with the Electronic Frontier Foundation that Utah's law on VPNs — tools that hide where your internet connection comes from — demands something that can't technically be done.

title: Black Forest Labs releases FLUX 3 Image
summary: Black Forest Labs, the company behind the FLUX family of image generators, has published FLUX 3 Image, its new image model.

title: ChatGPT gets a "Sites" feature
summary: OpenAI has a new feature page for Sites in ChatGPT, which drew wide attention on Hacker News today.

title: AstaBrief: an open model for writing research reports with sources
summary: The Allen Institute for AI open-sourced AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model inside its Asta research assistant.

title: AutoSynthData: making practice tasks for workplace AI agents
summary: ServiceNow described AutoSynthData, a system that generates training tasks for AI agents working inside enterprise software.

title: The case for hard spending caps on everything
summary: Simon Willison, a widely read developer and AI commentator, argues that we are going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much every paid service — limits that stop spending outright rather than just sending a warning.

title: Federal judge calls Flock cameras "indiscriminate mass surveillance"
summary: A US federal judge described Flock's licence-plate camera network as indiscriminate mass surveillance, TechCrunch reports.

title: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, a "sovereign" open AI model
summary: German AI company Aleph Alpha released Kolibri, an open-weight model — one whose files anyone can download and run on their own servers.

title: Inside Anthropic's effort to give Claude a moral compass
summary: The New York Times looks at how Anthropic tries to instill moral values into its Claude models.

title: AI agents don't see the same web everywhere
summary: A write-up compares three AI agents working in two countries and finds the web they navigate is uneven across languages.

title: When an AI agent says "done" but the work isn't
summary: Microsoft published ThinkingBox on the Hugging Face blog, an approach for checking whether an AI agent actually achieved its goal.

title: How GitHub opens a million-line pull request
summary: GitHub explained how it rebuilt the code-change viewer in its Copilot app so it can open a pull request with a million changed lines and hundreds of inline review comments.

title: A redaction mistake reveals a Google data center's water and power use
summary: Local outlet 1011 Now reports that an improperly redacted document exposed water and electricity figures for Google's data center in Lincoln, Nebraska — numbers that were meant to stay hidden.

title: UK safety institute works to make AI test scores repeatable
summary: The UK's AI Security Institute and the EvalEval group described how they are making AI benchmark results reproducible, so a score one lab reports can be checked by someone else.

title: GitHub Universe 2026: checking AI-written code takes centre stage
summary: GitHub previewed ten talks from its upcoming Universe conference, with sessions on verifying code written by AI and on keeping software building blocks secure.

title: A free tool turns off Apple Intelligence on Macs and reclaims the space
summary: An open-source project shows how to switch off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and recover the disk space its AI models take up.

title: A software glitch leaves F1 drivers without power in Bahrain
summary: Formula 1 drivers were left frustrated over a software glitch in Bahrain that left them powerless, Motorsport.

title: A 125-billion-parameter model running on a single gaming graphics card
summary: A project called Strata claims to run Qwen 3.

title: Your AI agent passed once. Will it pass again?
summary: IBM Research wrote on the Hugging Face blog about measuring whether an AI agent succeeds consistently on the same task, not just once.
